title: This Goose Flies Over the Himalayas in Air Humans Can't Handle
subject: bar-headed goose

scenes.text: A goose flies over the Himalayas, in air that would drop most people.
Bar-headed geese have been tracked climbing as high as 7,290 meters.
Up there, the air holds roughly a third of the oxygen at sea level.
Scientists put them on a treadmill in a low-oxygen box. They kept running.
Their hearts and flight muscles are packed with extra blood vessels.
Climbing takes seven or eight hours, then they cross in a day. Wings powered by thin air.

description:
Bar-headed geese cross the Himalayas, reaching about 7,290 meters.
Their hearts and muscles have extra blood vessels that deliver oxygen.
Would you try that climb?
first_comment: Which animal do you think handles thin air best?
